question: The Forum of European Muslim Youth and Student Organisations (FEMYSO) organised its European Action Day against Islamophobia in September 2026 and its ‘Unite & Act’ event during the summer.

The latter reportedly formed part of the ‘EmpowerAction’ project, funded within the framework of ‘Tackle’, supported by the Commission’s Development Education and Awareness-Raising (DEAR) programme and involving a sub-granting mechanism administered by Avocats Sans Frontières.

However, a report by the French Ministry of the Interior on the Muslim Brotherhood and political Islamism in France, identifies FEMYSO as the youth branch of the Council of European Muslims and as a ‘structure for training high-potential cadres of the movement’1.

In October 2025, France, Austria and the Netherlands called on the Council to strengthen the traceability and scrutiny of EU funding in order to prevent it from benefiting organisations linked to Islamism or antisemitism. Can the Commission clarify: 1.
whether the ‘Unite & Act’ event received, directly or indirectly, funding from the DEAR programme through ‘Tackle’ and Avocats Sans Frontières?
what amount was awarded to FEMYSO for the ‘EmpowerAction’ project, and whether it will publish the corresponding grant agreement and the amounts of the ‘Tackle’ subgrants?
whether it intends to respond to the calls for greater traceability made by France, Austria and the Netherlands, and whether it has reviewed the funding granted, directly or indirectly, to FEMYSO?
Supporter2

Ministry of Interior, 2025, “Frères musulmans et islamisme politique en France“, p. 32. https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/actualites/dossiers-de-presse/publication-du-rapport-freres-musulmans-etislamisme-politique-en-france. This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Jean-Paul Garraud (PfE).
